correctness.rationale: The boundary-reduction equalities follow from homogeneous factoring and maximum modulus. Exact two-atom weights at phases ±π/3 annihilate the quadratic term, preserve constant and linear terms, and sum in absolute modulus to 2/sqrt(3), proving the upper bound for all complex Banach E. The scalar P=1/2+z-z²/4 has |P(e^{it})|²=27/16−(cos t−1/2)²/2, hence full norm 3sqrt(3)/4 and projected norm 3/2, attaining 2/sqrt(3). Equality in triangle plus stationarity forces all scalar extremizers to the stated orbit; coordinate-zero cases have ratio≤1. The standalone package checker verifies exact rational identities and 384 illustrative finite cases. No infinite claim relies on enumeration.
